pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On a load error the cache is unconditionally overwritten with nil, evicting a previously valid cached value (and a failed CDN result falls through with its error masked by the file read).

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock, so every concurrent cold-start caller serially reloads the manifest (thundering herd under exclusive lock).

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On load failure the cache is overwritten with nil (and errors are never cached), so a persistently missing/broken manifest is re-read under exclusive lock on every request.
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:90 — CDN response status code is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx body is decoded as a manifest and yields a misleading parse error.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:40 — Concurrency fix to GetWebAssets ships with no test at all; the package has no _test.go, so there is no concurrent-callers test run under -race to prove the data race is gone.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock, so every goroutine that misses at once re-reads the manifest one after another; no test checks that a cold cache loads only once.
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — A failed load overwrites a good cached value with nil (errors are cached too), and no test covers what the cache holds after an error.
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — Nothing tests the dev/prod cache split: prod should return the cached pointer, and dev should reload on every call.
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:104 — No tests for readWebAssets edge cases: bad JSON, missing entrypoints or app/dark/light, integrity mapping, and applying the CDN URL.

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock, so concurrent cold-cache callers queue and each redundantly re-read and re-parse the manifest (thundering herd).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and does an initial cache read under RLock, but after deciding the cache is empty it unconditionally acquires the write lock (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` / `defer Unlock()`) without re-checking `entryPointAssetsCache` under that write lock. This means multiple concurrent callers that all observe a nil cache before the first writer populates it will serialize on the write lock and can each redundantly perform the manifest read/parse work once they acquire the lock. This is a performance/thundering-herd issue, not a correctness bug, and it is grounded in the shown locking/check sequence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — In dev mode every request takes the exclusive lock and does file I/O plus JSON decode, serializing all page loads.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and, after an initial RLock/RUnlock, unconditionally takes an exclusive Lock for the remainder of GetWebAssets when it doesn’t early-return from cache. In dev mode (cfg.Env == setting.Dev), the early return is skipped, so every call will hold the exclusive lock while the function proceeds (including whatever file I/O/JSON decoding happens later), which serializes concurrent requests. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/concurrency concern in dev mode, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On read error the cache is set to nil, so every subsequent request retries the failing I/O under the exclusive lock with no negative caching.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows adding an RWMutex around the global `entryPointAssetsCache` and the initial read/lock pattern in `GetWebAssets`. It does not show any code that sets the cache to `nil` on read error, nor does it show the error-handling/cache-write logic at all. Therefore the claim about nil-ing the cache on error and causing repeated failing I/O cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — Write lock is held across the CDN HTTP fetch (currently dead since cdn is ""), which would block all callers for network latency if enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a write lock (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` with `defer Unlock()`) being held for the remainder of `GetWebAssets`, but the provided diff hunk does not show any CDN-related HTTP fetch or where such a fetch occurs. The finding’s specific claim that the lock is held across a CDN HTTP fetch (and that cdn is "") cannot be verified from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock, so every concurrent cold-start caller serially reloads the manifest (thundering herd under exclusive lock).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and does a read-lock check before taking the write lock, but after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` there is no second check of `entryPointAssetsCache`. As a result, multiple concurrent callers that all observe `nil` under the initial RLock will each later acquire the write lock one-by-one and proceed to (re)load the assets even if a prior goroutine already populated the cache. This is a performance/efficiency issue (unnecessary serialized reload), not a correctness defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — CDN fetch runs while holding the global write lock using http.DefaultClient with no timeout; a slow CDN blocks all GetWebAssets callers, bounded only by the first caller's ctx.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a global RWMutex and acquires the write lock (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(); defer ...Unlock()`) before the function’s main work begins, meaning the remainder of `GetWebAssets` will execute while holding the global write lock. That can serialize callers and make them wait if the subsequent work is slow. However, the specific claims about a “CDN fetch” and use of `http.DefaultClient` “with no timeout” are not shown in this diff snippet, so only the lock-holding concern is directly verifiable from the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On load failure the cache is overwritten with nil (and errors are never cached), so a persistently missing/broken manifest is re-read under exclusive lock on every request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds an RWMutex around the global cache and changes the read path to take an RLock, then a write Lock before computing. It does not show any code that overwrites the cache with nil on error, nor any code about caching/not caching errors. Also, repeated re-reading when `entryPointAssetsCache` is nil would have happened before this change as well; the diff doesn’t prove a new “overwrite with nil” behavior. The only verifiable change here is that cache-miss work now happens while holding an exclusive lock, but the finding’s specific claim about nil-overwrite/error caching isn’t grounded in the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:90 — CDN response status code is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx body is decoded as a manifest and yields a misleading parse error.

It does not show any CDN HTTP call, response handling, or manifest decoding logic, so the claim about not checking a CDN response status code cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:40 — Concurrency fix to GetWebAssets ships with no test at all; the package has no _test.go, so there is no concurrent-callers test run under -race to prove the data race is gone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new concurrency behavior (a global RWMutex guarding the global `entryPointAssetsCache` in `GetWebAssets`), but the PR diff does not add any tests to exercise concurrent callers or validate the cache behavior under `-race`. The claim that the whole package has no `_test.go` files isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the absence of any new/updated test code alongside this nontrivial change is a concrete review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock, so every goroutine that misses at once re-reads the manifest one after another; no test checks that a cold cache loads only once.

adjudication.rationale: In GetWebAssets, the code reads entryPointAssetsCache under an RLock, then on a miss takes the write lock (entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()) but does not re-check the cache after acquiring it. This means concurrent goroutines that all see a cold cache can each serialize through the write lock and potentially recompute/re-read the manifest even if a previous goroutine already populated the cache before they acquired the lock. That’s an inefficiency/concurrency design issue rather than a correctness bug. The claim about missing tests isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the missing double-check is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — A failed load overwrites a good cached value with nil (errors are cached too), and no test covers what the cache holds after an error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds an RWMutex and changes cache reads/locking in GetWebAssets. It does not show any code that assigns `entryPointAssetsCache` after a load attempt (successful or failed), nor any error-handling path that would overwrite a previously good cache with `nil` or cache errors. The claim about what the cache holds after an error and missing tests is not verifiable from the provided diff hunk.
